solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cortes possibly had one

indicators.note: possibly says the name Cortes is just one possible arrangement of these six letters

explanation.surface: The conquistador Cortés presumably travelled with a guard of soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: Cortes rearranged gives the answer, and the conquistador Hernán Cortés would indeed have had a guard of soldiers, so the whole clue is both definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A guard accompanying an important person for protection is called by this word.

clue.text: A boy and a girl

parts.note: Eric is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A boy and a girl, apparently a pair.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'A boy' but the charade runs ERIC then A; 'and' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is a female first name, so it fairly stands for a girl.

clue.text: Caught by wild desire

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
raving means wild, frenzied

explanation.surface: Someone gripped by a wild urge.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong longing for something, synonym of desire as a noun.

clue.text: Mention with hesitation the German going north to fish

indicators.note: in a down entry, going north means the whole string is written upwards, read backwards

parts.note: to mention is to tell
um is a sound of hesitation
der is German for the

explanation.surface: Someone haltingly names the German who has headed north to go fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going north' turns the whole run TELLUMDER backwards; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A red mullet is a food fish of the Mediterranean, an example of fish.

clue.text: "Respect", cried Surrey's first XI

indicators.note: cried means called out, so the following pieces are heard rather than read

parts.note: Surrey's first letter is S and a cricket XI is a team, so the words give S TEAM

explanation.surface: A Surrey cricket fan shouts their respect for the county's first eleven.
explanation.walkthrough: S plus TEAM, said aloud, sounds like the answer. Surrey is an English county with a famous cricket club.
explanation.definitionFit: Regard or admiration, a direct synonym of respect as a noun.

clue.text: So clever it hurts!

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means clever, bright
... as a verb means to sting or hurt, as in it ...

explanation.surface: So clever it hurts: someone painfully bright.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective meaning bright and a verb meaning to sting painfully.

clue.text: Understanding the directions for keeping cover

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: ENE is the compass point east-north-east, made of directions
a tent is a cover or shelter

explanation.surface: Grasping the instructions for keeping something covered.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is a friendly understanding or agreement, especially between nations.

clue.text: Empty fancy Miranda has to become an assistant

indicators.note: to become says the letters change into a new arrangement
empty means remove the inside, leaving only the outer letters of fancy

explanation.surface: Fancy-free Miranda has to become someone's helper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' leaves FY from fancy; FY with MIRANDA rearranged gives the answer; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: From Robinson Crusoe's servant, the phrase means a loyal general helper.

clue.text: I saw Latin girl taken in by composer

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: vidi is Latin for I saw, as in veni, vidi, vici
Val is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone recalls watching a Latin girl being duped by a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I saw Latin' is one piece: the Latin for 'I saw', from Caesar's famous boast.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio Vivaldi was an Italian baroque composer of The Four Seasons.

clue.text: Seadog has gin sling — he's putting it away!

parts.note: an old salt is a seasoned sailor, a seadog

indicators.note: sling means toss about, so the letters of gin are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An old sailor knocks back a gin sling with gusto.
explanation.walkthrough: A gin sling is a cocktail, but here 'sling' rearranges gin. 'putting it away' suggests drinking but means saving.
explanation.definitionFit: Salting money away means stashing it for later, so the word means putting it away.

clue.text: Babysitter?

parts.note: read literally, it is something a baby sits in, a raised seat for feeding

explanation.definitionFit: This tall chair with a tray is where an infant sits to be fed.

clue.text: She needs a hand with her work

definitions.text: She needs a hand with her work

parts.words: She needs a hand with her work
parts.note: read literally, her work is done on a client's hand, filing and polishing nails

explanation.surface: A busy woman asks for help.
explanation.definitionFit: A beautician who trims and polishes fingernails works on a customer's hand.

clue.text: Obsessive, the Tyneside way

parts.note: Tyneside is in the North East of England, NE
Rd is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: Someone obsessive in the manner of a Geordie.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside, around Newcastle, lies in North East England; 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A socially awkward person obsessed with a narrow interest; used as a noun for an obsessive.

clue.text: Messenger is a nurse, the darling!

definitions.meaning: the Greek origin of the word means messenger, as heavenly messengers are
nurses are often praised as such, a ministering kindly figure
a darling, sweet person is called one of these

explanation.surface: A messenger turns out to be a nurse, and a lovely one.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavenly messenger, a caring nurse and a sweetheart are all senses of this word.

clue.text: Sound quality of a bird's calls over short periods recorded

indicators.note: recorded suggests sound played back, so the pieces are heard rather than read

parts.words: a bird's calls over short periods
parts.note: a pigeon's calls are coos and short periods are ticks, giving A COOS TICKS

explanation.surface: The quality of a recording of birdsong made in brief bursts.
explanation.walkthrough: A + COOS + TICKS, said aloud, gives the answer. A tick is British slang for a moment; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The way a room carries noise is its sound quality, the property this word names.

clue.text: Ranch serving enchilada excludes the uninitiated

indicators.note: serving, as dishing up food, signals the letters of enchilada are rearranged
excludes means one letter is taken out of the dish name

parts.note: L stands for learner, one who is uninitiated, as on British L-plates

explanation.surface: A ranch serves enchiladas but turns away newcomers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excludes' drops L from ENCHILADA; 'serving' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacienda is a large estate or ranch in Spanish-speaking countries.

clue.text: The person that dressed Tom Cruise

definitions.text: The person that dressed Tom Cruise

indicators.note: dressed, as in arranged or set out, signals the letters of the film star's name are rearranged

explanation.surface: Who was responsible for the film star's wardrobe?
explanation.walkthrough: The actor's name rearranged gives the answer, and the whole clue also describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A costumier makes or supplies costumes, so would dress an actor.

clue.text: The afternoon shift at Crufts?

parts.note: Crufts is Britain's big dog show, so its shift would be a watch kept by dogs

explanation.definitionFit: On ships the short late-afternoon and early-evening duty periods carry this name.

clue.text: Trying to be sporting

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means tiring, trying
sporting a hat means having it on

explanation.surface: Attempting to be a good sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' is a link joining the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means tiring as an adjective and having on clothes as a verb form.

clue.text: Monotonous comment about yours truly

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to say is to comment
yours truly is a jokey way of saying me

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that the speaker is boring.
explanation.definitionFit: Samey is informal British for repetitive and lacking variety.

clue.text: Satie manuscript redirected to artist

indicators.note: redirected means sent a different way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A score by the composer Satie is forwarded to a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was a French painter, leader of the Fauves.

clue.text: Any serious international assembly originates here

definitions.text: Any serious international assembly originates here

indicators.note: originates points to where each word begins, its opening letter

explanation.surface: A claim that any major global summit begins in this continent.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of Any Serious International Assembly spell the answer, and the clue suggests the continent as their origin.
explanation.definitionFit: A continent, the largest on Earth, named as the place of origin.

clue.text: A religious society propagating social communities

parts.note: pi is informal for pious, religious
a culture is a society and its customs

explanation.surface: A church group spreads friendly fellowship.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiculture is beekeeping, rearing the social insects in their colonies.

clue.text: When gang stages a lock-in there's anxiety

indicators.note: a lock-in suggests the answer is shut away inside the words gang stages

explanation.surface: A gang barricading itself in causes worry.
explanation.definitionFit: Angst is a feeling of dread or anxiety.

clue.text: Pay for the terms of reference

definitions.meaning: a task's scope, its terms of reference

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means send money; the noun means the scope of a job.

clue.text: Confesses to girl breaking into railway stores

indicators.note: breaking into means entering, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to sing is slang for to confess to the police
Di is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl owns up to breaking into a railway warehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stores' is a verb in the sense needed: tracks where trains are stored.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidings are short tracks where rolling stock is kept, so they store trains.

clue.text: How partial success may be attractive

parts.note: a win is a success
some means part, not all

explanation.surface: How a modest achievement can be appealing.
explanation.walkthrough: Echoes the saying 'you win some, you lose some'; 'How' and 'may be' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Winsome means charming and appealing, a synonym for attractive.

clue.text: Things about which, by changing direction, one's keen to see

definitions.text: Things about which, by changing direction, one's keen to see

parts.words: Things about which, by changing direction, one's keen to see
parts.note: gun or telescope aimers are adjusted in direction to see keenly, and tourist spots are places one is keen to see

explanation.definitionFit: Attractions worth visiting, and aiming devices on guns, both carry this name.

clue.text: Immediate appeal for books

parts.note: to urge is to appeal earnestly
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A pressing request for reading matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Urgent means demanding instant attention, synonym of immediate.
